turns.user: List 3DCP mortars from the literature whose static yield stress after 60 minutes of rest exceeds 10 kPa.
turns.text:
I’ll check the literature for 3DCP mortars with reported static yield stress after the specified rest time, keeping measured values separate from estimates based on structuration rate.
The retrieval results include apparent matches with timing or unit inconsistencies. I’m checking the measurement records and plotted data before including them in the list.
The database supports a list of reported values and additional figure-derived values at the requested rest time. The export query was rejected because its statement checker treated punctuation inside a text label as a separator; I’ll remove that punctuation and retry.
The literature database identifies the following **3DCP mortars with static yield stress above 10 kPa after 60 minutes of rest**. These are literature measurements or figure readings, not model predictions.

**Values reported in tables or text**

| Paper / location | Mix → static yield stress at 60 min |
|---|---|
| [Matric suction and shape stability](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2022.127618), Table 2 | 10% silica sand replacement → **13.04 kPa**; 20% → **18.91 kPa**; 30% → **19.86 kPa** |
| [Waste-glass-activated geopolymers](https://doi.org/10.1080/21650373.2025.2529994), §4.3.2 | 50S/0F/50G → **15 kPa**; 50S/20F/30G → **21 kPa**; 50S/35F/15G → **34 kPa**; 50S/50F → **40 kPa** |

**Additional matches digitised from figures**

| Paper / location | Mix → approximate static yield stress at 60 min |
|---|---|
| [DOI: 10.1016/j.autcon.2020.103394](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.autcon.2020.103394), Fig. 16 | “Printed concrete mixture” → **16.0 kPa** |
| [Printing in air and underwater](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.conbuildmat.2023.134403), Fig. 6a–c | **Air:** G1_0.40WC_0.04HEC → **10.7**; G1_0.40WC_0.06HEC → **17.8**; G2_0.40WC_0.02WLG → **10.7**; G2_0.40WC_0.04WLG → **17.9**; G2_0.40WC_0.06WLG → **20.2 kPa**. **Underwater:** G1_0.40WC_0.06HEC → **14.5**; G1_0.40WC_0.08HEC → **16.7 kPa** |
| [DOI: 10.1016/j.jobe.2024.111740](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jobe.2024.111740), Fig. 7b | RH20 → **11.6 kPa**; RH25 → **14.0 kPa** |
| [3D-printed heavyweight concrete](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.matdes.2023.112246), Fig. 14, measured series | M0 → **40.9 kPa**; M100 → **55.2 kPa** |
| [DOI: 10.3151/jact.24.60](https://doi.org/10.3151/jact.24.60), Fig. 3 | 25MCW → **16.5**; 25MPW → **12.5**; 50MCW → **15.3**; 50MPW → **12.3 kPa** |

Figure-digitisation uncertainties are respectively **12%, 10%, 8%, 6%, and 15%** by row. The **10.7 kPa** entries therefore do not clearly exceed the threshold within that uncertainty. Methods also differ: the silica-sand study uses squeeze flow; the other listed studies use penetration-based measurements.
